extracted.intended_audience: aircraft manufacturers/applicants and FAA certification engineers responsible for certifying electronic flight instrument systems (EFIS) and related installations
extracted.subtask_description: Special conditions and certification requirements for installation of electronic flight instrument displays (EFIS) and protection from High Energy Radiated Electromagnetic Fields (HERF) for the Beech Model 55 series (and similar installations). Covers system analysis, reliability, human factors (legibility/warnings), HERF qualification, and acceptable methods of compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issuance of special conditions for novel/unusual designs
rubrics_metrics.description: Special conditions may be issued and amended, as necessary, as part of the type certification basis if the Administrator finds that the airworthiness standards designated in accordance with § 21.101 do not contain adequate or appropriate safety standards because of novel or unusual design features of an airplane or installation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special conditions become part of the type certification basis and are issued in accordance with § 11.49 after public notice as required by §§ 11.28 and 11.29(b). They may be applied to other airplanes for installation of similar equipment without further amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination to determine dependency and criticality
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems and associated components must be examined separately and in relation to other airplane systems to determine if the airplane is dependent upon its function for continued safe flight and landing, and if its failure would significantly reduce the capability of the airplane or the ability of the crew to cope with adverse operating conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each system/component identified by this examination as being one upon which the airplane is dependent, or whose failure would significantly reduce capability or crew ability to cope, must be designed and examined to comply with the special condition requirements (see subsequent items).

rubrics_metrics.name: No single failure or probable combination preventing continued safe flight
rubrics_metrics.description: It must be shown that there will be no single failure or probable combination of failures under any foreseeable operating condition which would prevent the continued safe flight and landing of the airplane, or it must be shown that such failures are extremely improbable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to systems/components identified as critical by the dependency examination. Demonstration may be by analysis, tests, or combination of methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: No single failure or probable combination causing significant capability reduction
rubrics_metrics.description: It must be shown that there will be no single failure or probable combination of failures under any foreseeable operating condition that would significantly reduce the capability of the airplane or the ability of the crew to cope with adverse operating conditions, or it must be shown that such failures are improbable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a separate tier from catastrophic prevention (previous item) and may be demonstrated with appropriate analysis and testing to show improbability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of crew warning information and minimization of hazardous crew actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Warning information must be provided to alert the crew to unsafe system operating conditions and to enable them to take appropriate corrective action. Systems, controls, and associated monitoring and warning means must be designed to minimize initiation of crew action which would create additional hazards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design warning cues and monitoring so that crew corrective actions are clear, actionable, and do not introduce new hazards; these cues are part of the analysis for crew capability to detect and respond to faults.

rubrics_metrics.name: Means of compliance: analysis and testing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance with the requirements of this special condition may be shown by analysis and, where necessary, by appropriate ground, flight, or simulator tests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The analysis must consider: (i) Modes of failure, including malfunction and damage from foreseeable sources; (ii) The probability of multiple failures, and undetected faults; (iii) The resulting effects on the airplane and occupants, considering the state of flight and operating conditions; and (iv) The crew warning cues, corrective action required, and the capability of detecting faults.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numerical analysis as supporting evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerical analysis may be used to support the engineering examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numerical methods are permissible but not mandatory; they can support qualitative or rational analyses when data allow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic display legibility under all cockpit lighting conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic display indicators, including those incorporating more than one function, must be easily legible under all lighting conditions encountered in the cockpit, including direct sunlight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because emissive CRT colors and intensities differ from reflective electromechanical displays and vary with ambient illumination, legibility must be demonstrated for the full range of cockpit lighting conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic displays must not inhibit primary attitude display and must provide equivalent sensory cues
rubrics_metrics.description: In any normal mode of operation, electronic displays do not inhibit the primary display of attitude; and incorporate sensory cues for the pilot that are equivalent to those in the instrument being replaced by the electronic display units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sensory cues include visual (and where applicable tactile/auditory) information equivalent to the replaced instrument to support pilot situational awareness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of at least one essential information display after failures
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic display indicators, including their systems and installations, must be designed so that one display of information essential to safety and successful completion of the flight will remain available to the pilot, without need for immediate action by any crewmember for continued safe operation, after any single failure or probable combination of failures that is not shown to comply with paragraph (a)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design redundancy or segregation so essential information remains available without immediate crew intervention following failures not shown to be extremely improbable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collective reliability requirement when replacing traditional instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: For installations where electronic displays take the place of traditional instruments, the reliability must not be less than that of the traditional instruments. This concerns the collective reliability of the traditional instruments rather than the reliability of a single traditional instrument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special condition requires requirements needed for certification to demonstrate that the collective reliability of the new installation matches or exceeds the traditional ensemble used for safe flight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rational methods for system safety assessment allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Rational methods for safety assessment of systems may be shown by the use of numerical analysis but it is not mandatory. In many cases, adequate data is not available for preparing a stand-alone numerical analysis. Therefore, a rational analysis based on identification of failure modes and their consequences is frequently an acceptable substantiation of compliance with the various required levels of system reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of rational (qualitative/structured) analyses that identify failure modes and consequences is acceptable, particularly in small airplane certification where data are limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: HERF qualification: systems performing critical functions must be protected
rubrics_metrics.description: Each system that performs critical functions must be designed and installed to ensure that the operation and operational capabilities of these critical functions are not adversely affected when the airplane is exposed to high energy radiated electromagnetic fields external to the airplane.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critical functions are those whose failure would contribute to or cause a failure condition preventing continued safe flight and landing. HERF requirements apply only to critical functions; examples include primary electronic flight displays and FADEC systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: HERF compliance demonstration: envelope or laboratory test options
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualification of systems that perform critical functions, as installed in aircraft, is required to the defined HERF environment (an external field-strength envelope) or, as an option, by a laboratory test at a fixed value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Option (1) — demonstrate operation under the specified HERF field-strength envelope (frequency/peak/average values listed). Option (2) — laboratory test demonstrating withstand of a peak of 100 volts per meter in the frequency range of 10 kHz to 18 GHz. When using the laboratory test option, no credit is given for signal attenuation due to installation.

rubrics_metrics.name: No credit for installation attenuation in lab HERF testing
rubrics_metrics.description: When using a laboratory test to show compliance with the HERF requirements, no credit is given for signal attenuation due to installation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lab tests must assume the full applied field at the equipment input; do not reduce test levels to account for expected installation shielding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixed-value test value and post-certification reassessment caution
rubrics_metrics.description: The fixed laboratory test value is 100 V/m (revised from previously used 200 V/m). Applicants opting for the fixed value laboratory test, in lieu of the HERF envelope, will be subject to post certification reassessment based on the finalized rule requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choosing the 100 V/m fixed test may make it difficult under post-certification reassessment to qualify installations without design upgrades; applicants should be cautioned that additional protection provisions and/or testing may be required later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary hazard analysis requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A preliminary hazard analysis must be performed by the applicant for approval by the FAA to identify electrical and/or electronic systems that perform critical functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The analysis must identify systems whose failure would prevent continued safe flight and landing; systems identified are candidates for HERF requirements. Service experience alone is not acceptable justification for omission.

rubrics_metrics.name: HERF compliance methods and limits of relying on similarity or service experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance with HERF requirements may be demonstrated by tests, analysis, models, similarity with existing systems, or a combination thereof. Service experience alone is not acceptable since such experience in normal flight operations may not include exposure to the HERF environmental condition. Reliance on a system with similar design features for redundancy is generally insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because redundant elements can be concurrently exposed to HERF, similarity or service history cannot by themselves show adequate protection; provide analysis/tests that address worst-case concurrent exposure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and application of modulation for HERF testing
rubrics_metrics.description: The modulation should be selected as the signal most likely to disrupt the operation of the system under test based on its design characteristics. If the worst case modulation is unknown, default modulations may be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested defaults: 1 kHz sine wave with 80% depth of modulation for 10 kHz–400 MHz; 1 kHz square wave with >90% depth from 400 MHz–18 GHz. For frequencies where unmodulated signals cause deviations, apply several different modulating signals with various waveforms and frequencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of acceptable system performance under HERF exposure
rubrics_metrics.description: Acceptable system performance is attained by demonstrating that the system under consideration continues to perform its intended function during and after exposure to required electromagnetic fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deviations from system specification may be acceptable but must be independently assessed for each application and approved by the FAA.
